info.title: NewsCatcher News API
info.description:
Search the news NewsCatcher has crawled in the last **30 days**, in every language: ranked by relevance, source authority and freshness, and
grouped into **stories** (the articles that report the same event), with a one-line summary of each article. To page through every article that matches a boolean query over the last
**365 days**, use `/articles`.

## Authentication

Send your API key in the `x-api-key` header of every request. Keys are created in the NewsCatcher platform. A missing or invalid key is answered with `401`.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | What it does | Charged |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` or `POST /search` | Ranked articles for a request in plain words or with keywords. | Yes, by effort |
| `GET` or `POST /articles` | Every article that matches a boolean query, newest first, to page through. | Yes, 5 NCC per successful request |
| `GET /stories/{story_id}` | Every article of one story. | Yes, 1 NCC per successful request |
| `GET /subscription` | Your plan, limits and credit balance. | No |

## Effort and credits

`effort` sets how much work goes into the ranking. A search is charged in **NCC** credits, by the effort you ask for, and only when it succeeds (`200`).

| Effort | What it does | Credits |
|---|---|---|
| `low` | Ranks by relevance, authority, coverage and freshness. Fastest. | 1 |
| `medium` (default) | Adds a cross-encoder rerank of the top stories. | 5 |
| `high` | Adds an LLM judgement of the top stories and merges the stories that report the same event. Slowest, best quality. | 10 |

A search that finds nothing is still charged. A request that is refused or fails (`401`, `402`, `403`, `408`, `422`, `429`, `500`, `503`) is never charged. A call of `/articles` costs 5 NCC when it
succeeds, whatever the page size or the number of results.

## Query

`q` is a request in plain words or keywords, in any language, up to 500 characters. Put an upper-case `NOT` before a term to drop the articles that mention it in
their headline, description or summary (`Apple NOT iPhone`). `languages`, `countries` and `sources` narrow the search; the time window is the last 7 days unless you set
`search_window` (for example `15m`, `2h`, `1d`).

## Limits

Your plan sets the requests per second (per effort level and in all), an optional daily limit, the most results per request (`limit`) and how far back you can search.
`GET /subscription` returns all of them. Over a limit you get `429` with a `Retry-After` header. A `search_window` longer than your plan's history is cut to it and the response
says `window.clamped`.

## Errors

Every error has the same body: `message` (what went wrong), `status_code` and `status` (a short label). Use the HTTP status to decide what to do:

| Status | Meaning | Retry the same request? |
|---|---|---|
| `401` | The API key is missing or invalid. | No |
| `402` | Your credit balance does not cover the search. | After topping up |
| `403` | The plan does not include what you asked for (a larger `limit` or `page_size`, an Enterprise field) or the key may not use this API. | No |
| `404` | Unknown story. | No |
| `408` | `/articles` only: the search ran out of time and was stopped. | Yes, with a narrower window, a smaller `page_size` or a simpler query |
| `422` | A parameter is missing, invalid or unknown, or the body is not valid JSON. | No, fix it first |
| `429` | A rate limit of your plan. | Yes, after `Retry-After` seconds |
| `500` | Something failed on our side. | Yes, and tell us the `Correlation-ID` |
| `503` | A part of the service is temporarily unavailable. | Yes, after a short wait |

Every response carries a `Correlation-ID` header (quote it to support) and an `X-Process-Time` header.

## Enterprise fields

`include` adds heavy fields to every result (`description`, `entities`, `sentiment`, `themes`, `translation`, `embedding`). They are part of the Enterprise plans;
other plans get `403` with `enterprise_field`.

get.description:
Ranked real-news articles for a request in plain words or with keywords, grouped into stories.

See [Effort levels](/news/effort-levels), [Filters and sorting](/news/filters), [Writing queries](/news/writing-queries) and [Credits and pricing](/get-started/credits-and-pricing).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to look for: keywords with AND/OR/NOT or a plain-language question, in any language. An upper-case `NOT` (`Apple NOT iPhone`, `NOT "model y"`) drops the articles whose headline, description or summary mention the term.

parameters.name: effort
parameters.description: How much work goes into the ranking, and the price: `low` ranks by relevance, authority, coverage and freshness (1 NCC); `medium` adds a cross-encoder rerank of the top stories (5 NCC); `high` adds an LLM rerank and merges stories about the same event (10 NCC). Charged only when the search succeeds.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of articles to return (1 to 100; a plan may allow fewer, e.g. 50 on Free: the request is refused with 403 above it).

parameters.name: collapse
parameters.description: `diverse` (default) discounts repeated articles of one story, `story` keeps one article per story, `duplicates` keeps every article (copies of one article are always one result).

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: The order of the results: `relevancy` (default) best match first; `published_at` newest publication first; `crawled_at` newest crawl first. A date order covers the best matches of `q` (at least 100, or 5 times `limit`), not every article of the window, and `collapse=diverse` then keeps every article, as `duplicates` does. A publication date later than the crawl date counts as the crawl date.

parameters.name: search_window

schema.description: A number and a unit: minutes (`m`, `min`, `minute`, `minutes`), hours (`h`, `hr`, `hour`, `hours`), days (`d`, `day`, `days`) or weeks (`w`, `week`, `weeks`).

parameters.description: How far back to search, counted from now and measured on the publication date: a number and a unit, for example `15m`, `2h`, `1d`, `15 minutes`, `2 hours`, `1 day` or `1w`. From 1 minute up to your plan's history (30 days on the free plan; a longer request is cut to it and the response says `window.clamped`). Default: `7d`.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description: Only search these publishers: domains, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). Matches any copy of an article. The result then shows the requested domain: its name, and a link of that domain (with several matching domains on one article, the first of them in the article's order).

parameters.name: languages

items.description: ISO 639-1 language code; Chinese is `cn` (simplified) or `tw` (traditional), `zh` means `cn`.

parameters.description: Only articles in these languages: ISO 639-1 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). `zh` is searched as `cn`.

parameters.name: countries
parameters.description: Only articles from publishers in these countries: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100).

parameters.name: not_sources
parameters.description: Leave out these publishers: domains, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). An article is dropped when any of its copies comes from one of them.

parameters.name: not_languages

items.description: ISO 639-1 language code; Chinese is `cn` (simplified) or `tw` (traditional), `zh` means `cn`.

parameters.description: Leave out articles in these languages: ISO 639-1 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). `zh` is excluded as `cn`.

parameters.name: not_countries
parameters.description: Leave out articles from publishers in these countries: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100).

parameters.name: min_newsrooms
parameters.description: Only stories carried by at least this many newsrooms.

parameters.name: content_type
parameters.description: `news` (default) keeps real news articles only; `all` returns every article, whatever its type.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Heavy fields to add to every result, comma-separated or as an array: description, entities, sentiment, themes, translation, embedding. Enterprise accounts only (403 `enterprise_field` otherwise).

200.description: The articles, best first. `count` is 0 and `results` empty when nothing matched.

get.summary: List the articles that match a query
get.description:
Every article that matches a boolean query, newest first, for you to page through: the last 12 months, with the publisher, the date, the language, the country and a short snippet of
each. Use `/search` to find the best articles for a question; use `/articles` to get all the articles that match your query.

**Query.** `q` takes `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses, `"exact phrases"`, `+must`, `-mustnot`, `wild*cards` and `NEAR("a", "b", 5)`. `search_in` chooses where it is searched: the headline, the
body, both (default) or the summary, in the original language or in the English translation.

**Window and paging.** `from_date` and `to_date` set the window (the last 7 days by default, up to 365 days back: an earlier `from_date` is cut to it and the response says `window.clamped`).
`to_date` defaults to the moment of the request and is returned in `window.to`: send it back as `to_date` when you page, so every page covers the same articles. A page holds up to 100
articles and a query reaches its first 1,000 (`page` x `page_size` is at most 1,000). `total_hits` is the exact number of articles that match in the window.

**Filters.** `languages`, `countries`, `sources`, `predefined_sources` (`top 100 US`), the rank of the publisher (`ranked_only`, `from_rank`, `to_rank`) and the number of words narrow the
search; `not_languages`, `not_countries` and `not_sources` leave articles out. Copies of an article are returned too, unless you ask for `exclude_duplicates`.

**Credits.** A successful call (`200`) costs 5 NCC, whatever the page size or the number of results, also when nothing matches. A refused or failed request is not charged.
Your balance and limits are in `GET /subscription`.

**Two ways to call it.** `GET /articles` with the parameters in the query string, or `POST /articles` with the same parameters as a JSON body. In both, the list parameters take a
comma-separated string; in the JSON body they can also be arrays.

parameters.name: q

examples: "interest rate" AND (cut OR hike) NOT crypto

parameters.description: The boolean query: `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses, `"exact phrases"`, `+must`, `-mustnot`, `wild*cards` and `NEAR("a", "b", 5)` (the words within 5 of each other). Terms and phrases are searched in the fields of `search_in`.
parameters.example: "interest rate" AND (cut OR hike) NOT crypto

parameters.name: search_in
parameters.description: Where `q` is searched, comma-separated or as an array (at most 2): `title`, `body`, `title_body` (default), `summary`, and the same on the English translation: `title_translated`, `body_translated`, `title_body_translated`, `summary_translated`. A match anywhere in the article counts; the response carries the fields listed in `results`.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Start of the window: ISO 8601 (`2026-10-03`, `2026-10-03T14:00:00`, with or without an offset; UTC otherwise) or a phrase such as `7 days ago`. Default: midnight 7 days ago. Up to 365 days back (an earlier start is cut to it and the response says `window.clamped`).

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: End of the window, in the same formats. Default: the moment of the request. The response returns it in `window.to`: send it back when paging, so every page covers the same articles.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description: Only these publishers: domains, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). A domain with a subdomain (`news.bbc.co.uk`) matches that subdomain only.

parameters.name: not_sources
parameters.description: Leave out these publishers: domains, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). Only bare domains (`cnn.com`) leave anything out; a list made of subdomains only (`edition.cnn.com`) excludes nothing.

parameters.name: predefined_sources
parameters.description: Only the best-ranked publishers of a country or of the world: `top <n> <country code>` or `top <n> global`, for example `top 100 US`; combined with `sources`.

parameters.name: languages

items.description: ISO 639-1 language code; Chinese is `cn` (simplified) and `tw` (traditional), `zh` means both.

parameters.description: Only articles in these languages: ISO 639-1 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). `zh` means `cn` and `tw`.

parameters.name: not_languages

items.description: ISO 639-1 language code; Chinese is `cn` (simplified) and `tw` (traditional), `zh` means both.

parameters.description: Leave out articles in these languages: ISO 639-1 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). `zh` means `cn` and `tw`.

parameters.name: countries
parameters.description: Only articles from publishers in these countries: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). Ignored when `sources` is set.

parameters.name: not_countries
parameters.description: Leave out articles from publishers in these countries: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). Ignored when `sources` is set.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: The order of the results: `published_at` (default) newest first, `-published_at` oldest first, `relevancy` best match first, `rank` best-ranked publisher first.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, from 1. `page` x `page_size` is at most 1,000: a query returns up to its first 1,000 articles.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Articles per page (1 to 100; a plan may allow fewer: the request is refused with 403 above it).

parameters.name: ranked_only
parameters.description: Only articles from publishers that have a rank.

parameters.name: from_rank
parameters.description: Only publishers ranked at this position or lower (a larger number): the rank is the publisher's traffic rank, 1 being the best. 1 to 999999. Combined with `sources`, an article that matches either passes.

parameters.name: to_rank
parameters.description: Only publishers ranked at this position or better (a smaller number). 1 to 999999.

parameters.name: word_count_min
parameters.description: Only articles of at least this many words (`0` is a filter too: articles without a word count are left out); must be lower than `word_count_max`.

parameters.name: word_count_max
parameters.description: Only articles of at most this many words.

parameters.name: exclude_duplicates
parameters.description: Leave out copies of an article that another publisher published first. Off by default: the endpoint returns every match. Needs a window that starts after 2024-05-13 for English only (`languages=en`) and after 2025-03-17 otherwise.

200.description: The articles of the page, in the order of `sort_by`. `count` is 0 and `results` empty when nothing matched.

Every article that matches a boolean query, newest first, for you to page through: the last 12 months, with the publisher, the date, the language, the country and a short snippet of
each. Use `/search` to find the best articles for a question; use `/articles` to get all the articles that match your query.

**Query.** `q` takes `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses, `"exact phrases"`, `+must`, `-mustnot`, `wild*cards` and `NEAR("a", "b", 5)`. `search_in` chooses where it is searched: the headline, the
body, both (default) or the summary, in the original language or in the English translation.

**Window and paging.** `from_date` and `to_date` set the window (the last 7 days by default, up to 365 days back: an earlier `from_date` is cut to it and the response says `window.clamped`).
`to_date` defaults to the moment of the request and is returned in `window.to`: send it back as `to_date` when you page, so every page covers the same articles. A page holds up to 100
articles and a query reaches its first 1,000 (`page` x `page_size` is at most 1,000). `total_hits` is the exact number of articles that match in the window.

**Filters.** `languages`, `countries`, `sources`, `predefined_sources` (`top 100 US`), the rank of the publisher (`ranked_only`, `from_rank`, `to_rank`) and the number of words narrow the
search; `not_languages`, `not_countries` and `not_sources` leave articles out. Copies of an article are returned too, unless you ask for `exclude_duplicates`.

**Credits.** A successful call (`200`) costs 5 NCC, whatever the page size or the number of results, also when nothing matches. A refused or failed request is not charged.
Your balance and limits are in `GET /subscription`.

**Two ways to call it.** `GET /articles` with the parameters in the query string, or `POST /articles` with the same parameters as a JSON body. In both, the list parameters take a
comma-separated string; in the JSON body they can also be arrays.

q.description: The boolean query: `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses, `"exact phrases"`, `+must`, `-mustnot`, `wild*cards` and `NEAR("a", "b", 5)` (the words within 5 of each other). Terms and phrases are searched in the fields of `search_in`.
examples: "interest rate" AND (cut OR hike) NOT crypto

search_in.description: Where `q` is searched, comma-separated or as an array (at most 2): `title`, `body`, `title_body` (default), `summary`, and the same on the English translation: `title_translated`, `body_translated`, `title_body_translated`, `summary_translated`. A match anywhere in the article counts; the response carries the fields listed in `results`.

from_date.description: Start of the window: ISO 8601 (`2026-10-03`, `2026-10-03T14:00:00`, with or without an offset; UTC otherwise) or a phrase such as `7 days ago`. Default: midnight 7 days ago. Up to 365 days back (an earlier start is cut to it and the response says `window.clamped`).

to_date.description: End of the window, in the same formats. Default: the moment of the request. The response returns it in `window.to`: send it back when paging, so every page covers the same articles.

sources.description: Only these publishers: domains, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). A domain with a subdomain (`news.bbc.co.uk`) matches that subdomain only.

not_sources.description: Leave out these publishers: domains, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). Only bare domains (`cnn.com`) leave anything out; a list made of subdomains only (`edition.cnn.com`) excludes nothing.

predefined_sources.description: Only the best-ranked publishers of a country or of the world: `top <n> <country code>` or `top <n> global`, for example `top 100 US`; combined with `sources`.

items.description: ISO 639-1 language code; Chinese is `cn` (simplified) and `tw` (traditional), `zh` means both.

languages.description: Only articles in these languages: ISO 639-1 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). `zh` means `cn` and `tw`.

items.description: ISO 639-1 language code; Chinese is `cn` (simplified) and `tw` (traditional), `zh` means both.

not_languages.description: Leave out articles in these languages: ISO 639-1 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). `zh` means `cn` and `tw`.

countries.description: Only articles from publishers in these countries: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). Ignored when `sources` is set.

not_countries.description: Leave out articles from publishers in these countries: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). Ignored when `sources` is set.

sort_by.description: The order of the results: `published_at` (default) newest first, `-published_at` oldest first, `relevancy` best match first, `rank` best-ranked publisher first.

page.description: Page number, from 1. `page` x `page_size` is at most 1,000: a query returns up to its first 1,000 articles.

ranked_only.description: Only articles from publishers that have a rank.

from_rank.description: Only publishers ranked at this position or lower (a larger number): the rank is the publisher's traffic rank, 1 being the best. 1 to 999999. Combined with `sources`, an article that matches either passes.

to_rank.description: Only publishers ranked at this position or better (a smaller number). 1 to 999999.

word_count_min.description: Only articles of at least this many words (`0` is a filter too: articles without a word count are left out); must be lower than `word_count_max`.

word_count_max.description: Only articles of at most this many words.

exclude_duplicates.description: Leave out copies of an article that another publisher published first. Off by default: the endpoint returns every match. Needs a window that starts after 2024-05-13 for English only (`languages=en`) and after 2025-03-17 otherwise.

A date order covers the best matches of `q` (at least 100, or 5 times `limit`), not every article of the window, and `collapse=diverse` then keeps every article, as `duplicates` does. A publication date later than the crawl date counts as the crawl date.
